Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 103, verse 1–3:

(p-685) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-'Asr (the Declining Day / Time)

It is Meccan.

The Exalted and Majestic One said:

﴿By time (al-'asr)﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ ﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised one another to truth and advised one another to patience﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "al-'Asr" is the age (al-dahr). It is said of it: 'asr and 'usur, with the 'ayn and the sad vowelled with a damma. Imru' al-Qays said:

؎ ....... Will the ones who lived in the bygone age ever return?

Qatada said: "al-'Asr" is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy). Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ about al-'Asr, and he said: 'Your Lord swears by the end of the day.'" Some scholars, and Abu 'Ali mentioned it, said: al-'Asr is the day, and al-'Asr is the night, and from this is the saying of Humayd:

؎ The two 'asrs will not delay: a day and a night, ∗∗∗ if they seek to overtake what they have aimed at.

(p-686) Some scholars said: al-'Asr is the morning (bukra), and al-'Asr is the evening (ashiyya), and these are the two cool times (al-abradan). Muqatil said: al-'Asr is the Middle Prayer (al-salat al-wusta), by which Allah the Exalted swears.

"Al-insan" (mankind) is a generic noun. "Al-khusr" means deficiency and bad condition. This is quite clear regarding the disbeliever: he has lost this world and the Hereafter, and that is the manifest loss. As for the believer—although he may be in loss in his worldly life, in his old age and in what he endures of the hardship of this abode—he is pardoned in respect of his success in the Hereafter and his profit that does not perish. Whoever, throughout the span of his life, is engaged in mutual counsel to truth, patience, and acting in accordance with the counsels, no loss is with him, and all good has been gathered for him.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: "Wal-'asr, wa nawa'ib al-dahr, inna al-insana"; and in the codex of 'Abdullah: "Wal-'asri, laqad khalaqna al-insana fi khusr"; and it is narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited: "Inna al-insana lafi khusr, wa innahu fihi ila akhir al-dahr, illa alladhina"; 'Asim and al-A'raj recited: "lafi khusur" with a damma on the sin; Salam Abu al-Mundhir recited: "wal-'asr" with a kasra on the sad, and "wal-sabir" with a kasra on the ba'; and this is not permissible except in pausal form (al-waqf) by transferring the vowel (naql al-harakah). It is narrated from Abu 'Amr: "bil-sabr" with a kasra on the ba' as an 'ishmam (partial vowel), and this too occurs only in pausal form.

The tafsir of Surat [al-'Asr] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
